steps.message:
Curve-type notation for vertical electrical sounding (VES): take the layer resistivities in depth order. For each group of three consecutive layers (layers 1-2-3, then 2-3-4, and so on), write one letter: A if r1 < r2 < r3; Q if r1 > r2 > r3; H if r1 > r2 < r3; K if r1 < r2 > r3. A curve with N layers gets N-2 letters, in depth order (for example, a 4-layer curve gets 2 letters, such as HA). If all the letters are the same, the curve may also be written as that single letter (AAA may be written A).

Station T-19, survey area T. Interpreted layer model:

Layer | Resistivity (ohm-m) | Thickness (m) | Depth to base (m)
----- | ------------------- | ------------- | -----------------
1 | 609.2 | 25.53 | 25.53
2 | 7309.9 | 22.02 | 47.55
3 | 4367.7 | 0.42 | 47.97
4 | 4556.7 | - | -

The survey interpretation on file classifies this station's curve as KH-type.

Is this label correct for these layer values? Give a short answer, then end with one JSON line exactly like this:
{"label_correct": true or false, "curve_type": "<letters>"}

To determine the correct curve-type notation, we evaluate the resistivities of the four layers in groups of three:

1.  **First triplet ($\rho_1, \rho_2, \rho_3$):** 609.2, 7309.9, 4367.7.
    Since $609.2 < 7309.9 > 4367.7$, this follows the pattern $\rho_1 < \rho_2 > \rho_3$, which is the letter **K**.

2.  **Second triplet ($\rho_2, \rho_3, \rho_4$):** 7309.9, 4367.7, 4556.7.
    Since $7309.9 > 4367.7 < 4556.7$, this follows the pattern $\rho_2 > \rho_3 < \rho_4$, which is the letter **H**.

Combining these, the curve-type notation is **KH**.

{"label_correct": true, "curve_type": "KH"}
